extension.description: Standalone Chaturbate Kodi addon with priority-based TV mode, local favorites, and HLS playback through a localhost rewriting proxy.
extension.news: 0.7.55 - photo_set ListItem setArt is now thumb-only (drops icon + fanart). v0.7.54's per-phase timing immediately paid for itself: the morning after shipping, an identical hang recurred at 2026-05-29 01:42 CDT and the new instrumentation proved view_model_info itself ran in 316ms -- the lockup was DOWNSTREAM. The smoking gun was in kodi.log: at 01:42:55 view_model_info completed; at 01:42:56 "OutputPicture - timeout waiting for buffer" started firing at 18 messages per second; 22 seconds later InputStreamAdaptive's chunklist fetch from the in-process hls_proxy hit its CURL timeout; 56 seconds later "ActiveAE - large audio sync error: 52820 seconds" (14.7 hours of audio buffer drift -- the buffer was wedged in an impossible state). Root cause: every photo_set ListItem called setArt with three keys -- thumb, icon, fanart -- ALL pointing at the same Chaturbate-hosted cover URL. For a model with 17 photo_sets, that meant 51 simultaneous thumbnail HTTP fetches the moment view_model_info's directory rendered. Kodi's texture cache thread saturated, the video decoder thread was starved of CPU/IO, frame-buffer timeouts cascaded, the audio pipeline desynced, and the UI froze for 56+ seconds until the texture queue drained. model_d was the consistent repro (highest photo_set count tested). Fix is one line: only the thumb slot gets the URL now. Visual impact: icon falls back to a generic gradient (same icon used by all unstyled ListItems), fanart falls back to addon-default. Functionally identical for the user; 3x reduction in fetch storm. TDD: new regression test pins setArt() to exactly the {'thumb'} key set so this can never regress. Net: 774 -> 775 tests, +1 fetch-storm guard. Lesson: ListItem.setArt with N keys triggers N parallel texture fetches, not 1 -- one URL is loaded N times. For paywalled/uncached thumbs over the network, use one slot and let the others fall back.

0.7.54 - Per-phase timing instrumentation inside view_model_info + _render_view_model_info so the next slow-render lockup pinpoints its blocker. Trigger: real-world hang 2026-05-29 01:19 CDT on slug model_d while a playvid stream was live. User opened View Info, the dialog sat for ~70s, InputStreamAdaptive timed out twice on chunklist fetches (the in-process hls_proxy was starved because the same CPython script was blocked on view_model_info), then the dialog finally rendered and the player gave up with BrokenPipe. The existing "starting" log fired but there was no completion log + no per-step timing, so the cause (DB slow, fetch_biocontext hung, image_for_row, render loop?) was unknowable post-hoc. Fix is pure instrumentation: time.monotonic() stamps before each phase, consolidated "view_model_info: done slug=X total_ms=N k=v..." line at exit. Phase keys: db_open_ms, get_model_ms, fetch_bio_ms, upsert_bio_ms, get_model2_ms, render_ms (only present when their phase actually ran -- skipped phases are omitted to keep the line compact). Render side emits its own "_render_view_model_info: done slug=X render_total_ms=N image_ms=N add_items_ms=N end_of_dir_ms=N photo_sets=N" so a slow render is distinguishable from a slow DB or fetch. The 95MB model_meta.db on bcore makes a sqlite lock or large-row read plausible suspects, but the data tells us which without re-running the user's session. Three new TDD regression tests pin (a) done line emits with required keys on the cached-row path, (b) fetch_bio_ms appears when inline biocontext fires, (c) render-side done line emits with required keys. Net: 771 -> 774 tests, +3 instrumentation guards. No behavior change beyond logging. Lesson: every user-visible action handler should emit a phase-timing summary on exit -- "starting" alone is not enough when the cause of a future hang is unknown.

0.7.53 - Stale-stamp filter for the v0.7.52 post-Stop wedge watchdog. The v0.7.52 fix shipped 09:21 CDT and within 90min was killing HEALTHY streams: 6 false-positive POST-STOP-WEDGE trips between 10:11 and 10:33, TV mode exited via consecutive_stalls=5/5 (reason='stalls_exhausted'). Root cause: Window(10000).chaturbatetv_force_stop_at persists across iter rotations -- it lives on the Kodi-global window object, not per-iter local state. Each iter's hls_proxy fires force_player_stop on its way out (terminal-flag reconnect, or shutdown), stamping the prop. The NEXT iter starts a fresh play with a different slug + port, immediately reads the previous iter's stamp, and within 30s grace _is_stop_wedged trips on a perfectly healthy stream. iter=3 was killed 16s after onAVStarted because the stamp it adopted was 31s old (from iter=2's exit). iter=8 was killed 5s into the iter because it adopted a 401s-old stamp from a force_player_stop fired 6.7min earlier. Fix: new pure helper _select_stop_signal(new_stop_at, play_start_at) -> float|None filters out stamps strictly older than the current play's start time. Stamps >= play_start_at are in-session and treated as real signals; older ones are zeroed to None. Inclusive boundary handles microsecond-jitter for stamps written within the same instant. The inner monitor loop captures play_start_at = time.time() at the top, just before the while-loop, and passes it through _select_stop_signal on every tick. Real wedges (the v0.7.52 production incident at 01:16:56) still trip cleanly because their stamps come AFTER the wedged iter's play_start_at. Four new pure-function tests pin none-input/stale-filtered/fresh-passes-through/exact-equal-edge. Net: 767 -> 771 tests, +4 stale-stamp guards. Lesson: any Kodi-global Window prop used as a signal between addon processes needs an explicit session-scope filter; persistence across iters is silent unless designed against.

0.7.52 - Post-Stop wedge watchdog: detect when force_player_stop fires but isPlaying never flips false. Production wedge 2026-05-17 01:16:56 CDT: hls_proxy fired PlayerControl(Stop) 3 times in 50s after a 5-attempt reconnect GIVE UP on a tier slug, but Kodi's player never honored ANY of them. isPlaying() stayed True forever, the inner monitor loop's while-loop never exited, no heartbeat for 7+ hours, Kodi UI stuck on a busy spinner. Root cause: PlayerControl(Stop) is fire-and-forget. When Kodi's main thread wedges (libcurl hang, decoder lockup), the stop request is queued but never processed. The existing v0.7.41 stall watchdog (getTime advancement) and v0.7.50 caching watchdog (Player.Caching) both query the *player* for state, so when the player itself is unresponsive, neither trips. Fix: hls_proxy._force_player_stop now stamps Window(10000).chaturbatetv_force_stop_at with the current epoch right after firing the Stop. The tv_loop inner monitor loop reads the timestamp every tick and trips POST-STOP-WEDGE if isPlaying() is still True 30s past the most recent stamp. Recovery path is the same as the v0.7.41/v0.7.50 watchdogs: stall_detected=True + break the inner loop. The signal crosses Kodi processes (hls_proxy runs in the playvid-spawned process; tv_loop runs in the TV mode service process) via the Kodi-global Window object. Latest-stamp-wins semantics: rapid-fire stop requests (3-in-50s observed) update the timestamp each call so we measure against the freshest request, not the first. Six pure-helper tests pin the state machine: no-request/not-playing/within-grace/past-grace/recovery/latest-wins. Net: 767 tests, +6 stop-wedge guards. Discovered the morning after the wedge - Kodi-the-process alive, kodi.log still ticking, but chaturbatetv addon process hung on the busy spinner; recovery was systemctl restart kodi.service.
0.7.51 - Search dialog fix: clicking Search from the main menu now actually works. The shim (addon_actions.search) was invoked as a directory-load on a real Kodi handle, opened the dialog, then tried to redirect via xbmc.executebuiltin Container.Update with mode=search and the query. That redirect lost a race against Kodi's "GetDirectory failed -> navigate to parent" path, which fires implicitly whenever a directory-load handler returns without populating its handle. Live trace confirmed: Container.Update fired (logged in feature.log), but next dispatch was mode='' (main_menu) and kodi.log had the matching GetDirectory failed entry. Fix: on the submit path, populate THIS handle directly by calling browse_views.search_view(handle, query) - no redirect, no race. The cancel/empty-query path closes the directory cleanly via _close_directory_handle so Kodi clears its busy spinner. Tradeoff: breadcrumb URL stays as ?mode=search_prompt so hitting Back from results re-prompts; acceptable vs the prior "no results at all" failure. Also added logger calls (prompt opening / prompt closed query_len=N / invoking search_view) so the dispatch chain is traceable in feature.log. Confirmed the search API path itself was healthy via probe script: cb_endpoints.search_url + cb_client.fetch_browse_page + cb_listing.parse_roomlist returned ~100 valid Models per test query. Two regression tests pin (a) empty-query closes directory cleanly without Container.Update, (b) submit-query invokes search_view directly on the same handle without firing Container.Update. Net: 761 tests, +2 search-shim guards.
0.7.50 - Caching-wedge watchdog. Closes a real-world failure mode the v0.7.42 stall watchdog couldn't catch: a decoder freeze where audio creeps wildly out of sync (1603-89463s ActiveAE drift observed 2026-05-10 07:30 CDT) keeps getTime() advancing slowly, so the progress watchdog stays armed for the entire wedge -- 84 minutes on iter=15 in the live incident. Meanwhile Kodi already KNEW the stream was wedged: it was drawing a "Loading 25%" overlay via the Player.Caching condition. Fix reads that condition directly: xbmc.getCondVisibility("Player.Caching") and xbmc.getInfoLabel("Player.CacheLevel"), tracked per-tick (5s cadence) in the inner monitor loop. If Caching=True for >120s wall-clock, trip player.stall_detected=True and reuse the existing v0.7.42 stall recovery (mark slug offline, rotate). Transient buffer dips clear cleanly because the timer resets on Caching=False. State-tracking diagnostics: only logs on transitions ("Player.Caching=True ... watchdog grace 120s" / "Player.Caching=False (recovered after Ns)") so heartbeats stay clean. Pure helper _is_caching_wedged() is the test target -- 5 new pure-function tests pin first-seen-starts-timer, within-grace-no-trip, past-grace-trips, recovery-clears-timer, and never-caching-no-state. Also added xbmc.getCondVisibility to the type stubs (was already present in real Kodi but missing from tests/stubs/xbmc.pyi). Net: 759 tests, +5 caching-wedge guards. Discovered when the autonomous cron caught the user manually reporting a frozen-pic-but-UI-responsive state and we live-probed the xbmc API to confirm Player.Caching exists.
0.7.49 - Window-property TTL bump for silent-stub mark-offline. The v0.7.48 fallback used a 5.0s TTL on the playvid-stamped Window-property marker, but the actual zombie-stop race takes ~5+ seconds end-to-end (5 proxy reconnect attempts at ~1s each, plus the inner-loop exit-log overhead). Production wedge observed 2026-05-08 10:47 CDT: TV mode picked a P17 favorite, hit a 403 storm + reconnect-give-up; iter=2 silent-stub setResolvedUrl fired at 10:47:14, the OLD iter=1 zombie proxy fired its terminal+Stop at the SAME instant, iter=2 exited at 10:47:19 with tracked_file=None and dialog_id=10138 (busy spinner). Diff was exactly 5.0s -- the v0.7.48 TTL check ``diff >= 5.0`` returned True, the fallback returned empty, mark-offline was skipped, iter=3 re-picked the same offline slug, and Kodi wedged inside xbmc.Player().play(). Fix: bumped ``_SILENT_STUB_TTL_SEC`` from 5.0s to 15.0s. New regression test pins an 8s-old marker (was stale under v0.7.48, fresh under v0.7.49) to the True path so this exact race can't regress. Net: 754 tests, +1 TTL guard. Discovered by the autonomous log-check cron as it was happening live.
0.7.48 - Window-property fallback for silent-stub mark-offline. Real-world wedge observed: TV mode picked a model who had been live, hit a 403 storm + reconnect-give-up, then re-picked the same model in private show on the next iter. Silent stub setResolvedUrl fired correctly, but the OLD proxy from the previous iter fired its terminal+Stop at the SAME instant the silent stub was starting. Result: Kodi never fired onAVStarted for the stub (cross-process race), tracked_file stayed None, _was_silent_stub_played(None) returned False, mark-offline branch never ran, slug stayed in the cache, the loop re-picked the same offline slug on the next iter, and Kodi's player.play() eventually wedged inside an undismissible modal. The TV-list view froze on screen. Fix: playvid stamps Window(10000) properties ``chaturbatetv_silent_stub_slug`` + ``_epoch`` when serving the silent stub. _should_attempt_silent_stub_mark and _resolve_silent_stub_slug now check the marker as a fallback when the existing tracked_file / playlist-path signals don't resolve. Stale markers (>5s) are ignored to avoid false-positive mark-offline. Three new regression tests pin recent-marker fallback fires, stale-marker doesn't fire, and resolve_silent_stub_slug uses the marker when queue is ambiguous. Net: 753 tests, +3 silent-stub fallback guards.
0.7.47 - In-addon-switch guard so picking a different model from inside the addon (TV list, favs, etc.) while TV mode is playing doesn't get misclassified as a real user-stop and exit TV mode. Real-world repro: 2-member tier P10 [model_a, model_b] playing model_a; user navigated to TV list and picked model_b; Kodi fired Stop on model_a's playback (idle=0, model_a still live); decide_after_stop classified as "real user stop" -> exit; "TV mode exited" toast fired before onAVStarted got a chance to detect the takeover/switch. Fix: playvid handler stamps a Window property ``chaturbatetv_pending_play_epoch`` on the Kodi home window (id 10000, cross-process visible) at entry; _classify_after_stop checks it before returning ``user_stopped`` -- if the marker is <5s old, treat as a switch in flight and fall through (let onAVStarted's TAKEOVER vs internal-advance logic handle it). 5s window covers DNS + AJAX + prefetch latency for the new item to start. Three new regression tests pin recent-marker-falls-through, stale-marker-still-exits, and no-marker-unchanged behavior. Net: 750 tests, +3 in-addon-switch guards.
0.7.46 - Public release housekeeping: source URL in addon.xml now points at the GitHub repo (was a broken placeholder left over from internal-gitea hosting). No code change.
0.7.45 - TTL on the silent-stub session blocklist. Real-world repro (model_a): TV mode tried her at 17:05 while she was in private show (AJAX returned status='private', is_live=False); silent stub fired; ``_tv_bulk_mark_offline`` added her to ``_OFFLINE_SESSION_SLUGS``. She returned to public broadcast around 19:30 but every subsequent bulk_refresh kept logging "session-blocked 1" -- her -- while a lower-priority model played at P12 instead of her P17 tier. Pre-fix the blocklist was session-long: once added, a slug stayed filtered until tv_stop or process restart. The v0.7.33 anti-thrash intent was right (don't bounce on a model whose affiliate-feed status flips every TTL window), but the lifetime was too aggressive -- a model who legitimately recovered from private/hidden mode was still blocked. Fix: ``_OFFLINE_SESSION_SLUGS`` is now ``dict[str, float]`` (slug -> blocked-at epoch); ``_tv_bulk_refresh`` prunes entries older than ``_OFFLINE_BLOCK_TTL_SEC`` (15min) at the top of each refresh. After the TTL, the model gets a fresh chance on the next bulk fetch. Added log line "pruned N slugs from offline blocklist (TTL 900s elapsed)" for diagnostics. Net: 751 tests, +2 TTL regression guards. Discovered by user noticing model_a was online but TV mode hadn't promoted to her -- caught from the live system, not a hypothesis.
0.7.44 - Cross-process zombie-proxy guard. The v0.7.43 in-process guard via ``_active_proxy`` only caught siblings WITHIN one Python process. But each Kodi-spawned ``playvid`` runs in its OWN process, so ``_active_proxy`` is process-local: process B's zombie still sees ITSELF as the in-process active proxy. Real-world repro post-v0.7.43 (cron log check at 14:30): rapid model-switching model_a -> model_b -> model_c had three sibling proxies running across three playvid processes, and old proxies kept firing ``PlayerControl(Stop)`` when their reconnect-give-up exhausted -- killing whichever sibling proxy the player was actually serving. The fix uses ``xbmc.Player().getPlayingFile()`` -- a Kodi-global state visible across addon processes -- and bails when the player's URL doesn't contain this proxy's bound port token (``:PORT/``). Stashed the bound port on ``_State.port`` after server.bind() so the cross-process check has the comparison value. Net: 749 tests, +4 cross-process zombie guards. The v0.7.43 in-process guard is preserved as defense-in-depth for the test harness scenarios where one process holds two proxies. Discovered by the autonomous log-check cron's manual fire today -- it found multiple post-v0.7.43 ``force_player_stop`` firings with no corresponding "skipped" log line, proving the in-process guard wasn't catching the sibling-process case.
0.7.43 - Zombie-proxy guard for takeover playback. Real-world repro: TV mode plays model_a for ~9 minutes, user picks model_b from the TV List, takeover detection releases TV mode (v0.7.40 working) and model_b starts playing. But model_a's old proxy was still grinding through its 5-attempt 403-reconnect chain in a background thread. When that exhausted ~10 seconds later, it fired ``PlayerControl(Stop)`` -- which by then was hitting model_b's player, killing playback that had been working fine. Two layered fixes: (1) ``_force_player_stop`` checks ``_active_proxy._state is state`` and bails as a "supplanted zombie" if not. Defense against the late race where the old proxy reaches its give-up after the new one is already serving. (2) ``_stop_active_proxy`` now sets ``prev._state.stopping = True`` SYNCHRONOUSLY before spawning the daemon cleanup thread, so any in-flight reconnect on the old proxy bails on its next ``not state.stopping`` check rather than waiting (potentially seconds) for ``server.shutdown()`` to drain. Tests: zombie-state must not fire, active-state still fires, no-active-proxy edge-case still fires, stopping flag flips synchronously. Net: 745 tests, +4 zombie-proxy guards. Plus three pre-existing _force_player_stop tests now monkey-patch _active_proxy=None for explicit test isolation (other tests leaving the global set was masking the new guard's correct behavior).
0.7.42 - Stall watchdog hardening + smart rotation. Three fixes layered on the v0.7.41 watchdog: (1) FALSE-POSITIVE FIX: live HLS streams in Kodi+ISA frequently keep ``getTime()`` pinned at 0.0 even while playing fine -- the v0.7.41 watchdog couldn't tell those healthy streams from a wedged decoder and was killing model_a-style live sessions the user was actively watching. Fixed: only fire stall after we've seen the position advance past zero (last_position > 0.1). The "never advanced" case is left to the proxy's reconnect-and-give-up path (5 attempts, ~10s) which handles the no-segments-served branch separately. (2) MARK-OFFLINE-ON-STALL: when the watchdog DOES fire on a real stall, mark the stalled slug offline in the bulk-live cache so next pick_target picks a DIFFERENT model. Pre-fix, a single-model tier whose stream was genuinely frozen would re-pick the same slug forever, firing "Stream stalled" toasts in a tight loop. Bulk refresh re-adds the slug in ~10min. (3) CIRCUIT BREAKER: if 5 stalls fire back-to-back across iters (every model in reach is stalling), exit TV mode entirely with a "Many streams stalling" notification. Network is broken or Chaturbate is rejecting our edge connections; no point spinning. Plus diagnostic log: ``first-advance getTime()=N.NNs (elapsed=Ns); stall watchdog now armed`` so post-mortem can tell "stream never decoded" from "stream decoded then froze." Net: 741 tests, +3 stall guards.
0.7.41 - Stall watchdog for ISA-side decoder freezes. Pre-fix, a corrupt CMAF fragment from upstream (Chaturbate edge CDN occasionally serves segments where ProcessMoof can't find the TRAF atom) would freeze the inputstream.adaptive decoder while ``xbmc.Player().isPlaying()`` kept returning True. The inner monitor loop heartbeated ``playing=True`` forever on a stuck frame, and Kodi never fired ``onPlayBackStopped`` so TV loop never rotated. Repro: model_a stream, 17 minutes of clean playback, then ProcessMoof TRAF errors at decode time, then dead air. Fix: added ``tv_classify.is_progress_stalled`` (pure function, 9 tests covering the state machine), wired it into the inner monitor loop to watch ``getTime()`` per tick. If position hasn't advanced for 20s past a 10s grace window AND the player isn't paused, fire ``PlayerControl(Stop)``, set ``stall_detected``, and bypass ``_classify_after_stop`` so we always rotate to the next iter (never prompt "Exit TV mode?" on a stall, since idle could be 0 or high and either should mean "rotate"). User sees a "Stream stalled - moving on" notification. Net: 738 tests, +9 stall guards.
0.7.40 - Takeover-detection fix for single-model tiers. When the active TV tier held exactly one model and the user clicked a different model in browse, Kodi replaced the playlist with a one-item one (size=1). The pre-fix takeover-detection fallback was ``pl_size == len(queued_paths)`` -- 1 == 1 -- so the heuristic misclassified the user takeover as an internal advance and TV loop kept running invisibly underneath the user's click. Replaced with a queued-URL match: ``pl[pos].getPath() in queued_paths``, which is insensitive to playlist size and cleanly separates "ours" from "theirs." Net: 729 tests, +2 regression guards. Also: addon.xml now has a manifest-validation test gate so a malformed news entry can't ship green again (cf. v0.7.39 news incident).
0.7.39 - Security fixes from audit pass #5. 21 findings, 5 HIGH, all closed by 6 architectural changes. Net: 723 tests.
(1) **Host-allowlist function** ``cb_endpoints.is_trusted_url`` -- accepts ``https://`` URLs whose hostname ends with ``chaturbate.com`` / ``mmcdn.com`` / ``highwebmedia.com``. Used by hls_proxy._fetch (closes the SSRF via ``/segment?url=`` -- a sibling Kodi/Plex/Jellyfin process on the same box could previously read /etc/shadow or pivot to LAN admin pages through the proxy), addon_actions.show_picture (closes the ShowPicture builtin injection -- a malicious cover_url with ``)`` could chain another Kodi builtin), and model_meta_store.image_for_row (closes the Kodi-image-cache LAN pivot).
(2) **`_strip_bbcode`** helper applied at every render-boundary callsite for CB-controlled fields (real_name, about_me, wish_list_html, social_medias, last_subject, body_type, location, status, tag entries). Pre-fix, a malicious model with ``about_me="[/COLOR][COLOR FFff0000]CLICK https://evil[/COLOR]"`` could break out of the addon's color scheme and inject attacker-styled markup; rows with broken close-tags rendered invisible (Lesson 4 territory). The strip replaces ``[`` with ``(`` and ``]`` with ``)`` -- lossy but bounded, and tests verify the contract.
(3) **Inverted `_redact_url`** to log only ``scheme://host/path``, dropping query string + fragment entirely. Pre-fix, the redaction was an allowlist of 5 keys ({token, sig, session, auth, key}) which left Akamai/CloudFront tokens (hdnts, hdnea, Signature, Policy, KeyPair-Id, Expires) silently logged to disk. Inversion is maintenance-free against future CDN tokens. Plus: cb_client.fetch_browse_page and _default_fetch now route URLs through _redact_url before logging (pre-fix only hls_proxy used the redactor).
(4) **urlencode the search query** in ``addon_actions.search``. Pre-fix, a query containing ``)`` or ``,`` would break out of the ``Container.Update`` builtin and let a follow-up command run.
(5) **`_is_valid_slug`** regex (`[A-Za-z0-9_.]{1,64}`) at every slug-receiving entry point that mutates state or renders BBCode (fav_add, tv_add, playvid, refresh_one_model, view_model_info, show_profile). Reject early so a crafted slug can't reach a ``[B]NAME[/B]`` dialog (BBCode breakout) or interpolate CRLF into a Referer header (request smuggling, currently blocked by stdlib but defense in depth).
(6) **`RecursionError` catch + biocontext body-size cap (256 KB)**. Pre-fix, an adversarial deeply-nested JSON could raise RecursionError and crash a TV-loop iter; an oversized biocontext body could be stored verbatim in the DB (disk-fill DoS via the ``bio_full_json`` column).
20+ new tests covering: ``is_trusted_url`` allowlist matrix (apex, subdomains, file://, ftp://, javascript:, LAN pivots, lookalike-host bypasses), ``_fetch`` raises ValueError on untrusted URLs, ``show_picture`` rejects untrusted hosts AND URLs with builtin-breakout chars, ``image_for_row`` drops untrusted URLs and synthesizes only on alphanum slugs, log redaction strips Akamai-style tokens + URL fragments, search urlencode pins the query-encoding contract, slug regex rejects path-traversal/CRLF/empty.
Production code surface: 4 modules touched (cb_endpoints adds 30 lines, hls_proxy + addon_actions + model_meta_store get the new guards). ruff clean, mypy --strict clean.
0.7.38 - Error-handling and resource-leak fixes from audit pass #4. 12 fixes covering all 11 HIGH findings + the autocommit-perf MEDIUM. Net: 707 tests.
(1) router.py top-level handler wrap. Pre-fix, an exception in any view propagated uncaught -> Kodi showed "Plugin failed to start" toast and left the busy spinner spinning until ~30s timeout. Now: catch, log, call endOfDirectory(handle, succeeded=False), notify the user via xbmcgui.Dialog().notification with a NOTIFICATION_ERROR icon. handle=-1 from RunPlugin paths skips endOfDirectory.
(2) browse_views fetch-fail handling. _fetch_models used to propagate OSError up to view handlers; now catches and returns empty list with a log line. Listings render cleanly with no spinner-trap on network blips.
(3) parse_roomlist / parse_affiliate_onlinerooms log body snippet on JSONDecodeError. Pre-fix, Cloudflare HTML / rate-limit pages / login redirects all collapsed to "empty list" indistinguishable from "no live rooms". New _payload_snippet helper logs the first 120 chars of the body (whitespace-collapsed for one-line readability) so cb_feature.log shows the leading marker.
(4) favs_views distinguishes fetch-fail from "everyone offline". _classify_favs returns a third tuple element (fetch_failed bool); online_favs_view and offline_favs_view notify "network unreachable" via xbmcgui when set so the user can tell the network's down vs all 1228 favs are genuinely offline.
(5) screensaver win.show() failure short-circuits to None. Pre-fix, if show() raised the loop would block on a non-shown window forever; now bails immediately and the TV loop falls through to next iter.
(6) HLS proxy _harvest_segment_maps recheck refresh_gen. v0.7.37 added the gen-check at the chunklist handler's outer cache write but the per-line harvest writes still raced. Now harvest takes a gen_before kwarg, batches into a local dict, then bulk-updates under one lock with a final gen-check -- drops the data on the floor if a refresh landed mid-harvest. Bonus: replaces 100 per-line lock cycles with one bulk acquire.
(7) HLS proxy _run_reconnect terminal-flip under lock. Pre-fix, the if-needs_terminal-and-not-state.stopping check ran lockless between two locked blocks; concurrent stop() could fire PlayerControl(Stop) at the wrong moment. Single critical section now keeps stopping/terminal observed coherently with the decision they gate.
(8) model_meta_store _ensure_columns swallows duplicate-column race. Two concurrent first-launch upgrades both pass PRAGMA, both ALTER -- loser raises OperationalError("duplicate column name"). Pre-fix, the exception bubbled to caller's bare except and meta render silently degraded. Now: catch the specific message + log + continue.
(9) file_lock yields a sentinel bool. Pre-fix, OSError on os.open or fcntl.flock degraded silently to fail-open with no signal. Now yields False on acquire failure so callers can branch (notify, retry, or accept-and-document); existing call sites that ignore the value still get fail-open behavior, but the silent downgrade is now traceable.
(10) Orphan tempfile sweeper at load(). Kodi-SIGKILL between mkstemp and os.replace orphans .favs-*.json / .tv-*.json forever. Pass #1 agent 3 flagged this; never shipped until now. Sweep runs on every load() call, removes tempfiles older than 1h (bounded so concurrent in-flight saves aren't disturbed).
(11) deep_refresh DB-error early-bail. Pre-fix, sqlite OperationalError ("database is locked", schema mismatch, disk full) collapsed into the generic per-slug error count -- 20 minutes of work silent-failing on 1228 slugs with a "1228 errors" toast that gave no actionable signal. Now: catch sqlite3.OperationalError specifically, count consecutive occurrences, bail after 10 with a clear toast.
(12) model_meta_store upsert_rooms autocommit fix (MEDIUM promoted).
